sections.title: A8. Question for the next design stage

rows: How can we ensure that approval always uses the identity of the signed-in user?
The check currently uses the ID sent by the client. The test described in A3 confirmed that this check can be bypassed.

blocks.content: AI helped locate the relevant code and prepare the diagram. We ran 9 API tests against the running application and also verified the results in the database:

rows: The owner approves a pending reservation.
HTTP 200. The reservation changed to CONFIRMED; the confirmation time, a history record and a student notification were stored.
Another teacher and a student send their own IDs (2 tests).
HTTP 403. Reservations, history and notifications remained unchanged.
The owner approves an already confirmed or cancelled reservation (2 tests).
HTTP 409. Reservations, history and notifications remained unchanged.
A nonexistent reservation or user specified in the request (2 tests).
HTTP 404. The test data remained unchanged.
Another signed-in teacher sends the owner's ID when approving.
HTTP 200. Another teacher's reservation was confirmed — the authorization bug was reproduced.
Another signed-in teacher sends the owner's ID when cancelling a pending reservation.
HTTP 200. Another teacher's reservation was cancelled — the same bug was reproduced here as well.

blocks.content: We used temporary accounts and reservations and removed them afterwards. The authorization bug is recorded in A3 and has not been fixed yet.

sections.title: Change from the original version — actor identity

blocks.content: Previously, approve/cancel trusted actorUserId from the request body. The controller now passes the authenticated session identity, and the reservation service checks the active role, ownership and allowed state. A supplied actor ID is ignored. The frontend sends only the token and an optional note for these actions.

Verification: all 10 regression tests passed. Another teacher or student cannot act using a spoofed ID (403, with no reservation, history or notification changes). The owner can approve a pending reservation, and its student or teacher can cancel it. Approval of CONFIRMED/CANCELLED returns 409; unauthenticated requests are rejected.

Tests exercise the real filter → API → service path with mocked persistence and session validation. They do not re-verify persistence or concurrency. ADR-01, the before/after comparison and details are in docs/architecture-and-decisions.md and docs/evidence-and-evolution.md. This fix covers reservation approval and cancellation; other endpoints require separate review.
